To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the renal functional reserve in healthy older people is reduced; (2) the renal functional capacity of older patients is reduced compared with younger patients; (3) the renal functional deficit in patients is not due to atherosclerotic disease but to age-related changes in the kidneys; and (4) the renal functional deficits are due to a reduction in the renal vasculature and the glomeruli.

the renal functional reserve, as measured by the renal response to a maximal vasodilator stimulus, is impaired in healthy older subjects and is associated with an increase in the serum concentration of asymmetric dimethylarginine (ADMA), an endogenous inhibitor of nitric oxide synthase.
renal function and renal hemodynamics are impaired in the elderly.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding how aging influences the development of renal and cardiovascular disease.
the effects of aging on the renal function and the renal vascular function.
the role of the endothelium in the regulation of renal and vascular function in ageing and in the development of renal and vascular diseases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ageing is a risk factor for the development of renal disease and renal failure.
ageing is associated with a decrease in renal function and a decrease in renal reserve capacity, but the magnitude of this decrease is not large.
ageing is associated with a decline in the renal function of the elderly population, but this decline is not uniform in all age groups.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ageing process per se is not associated with a significant decline in the renal function, as measured by creatinine clearance, in the elderly.
ageing is associated with a reduction of renal function and renal blood flow, and that the renal reserve is decreased.
we found that the elderly are not different from younger patients in terms of renal function.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the elderly are not the same as the young.
we have to be very careful about how we use the creatinine clearance to estimate renal function in older people.
the kidney and the vascular system are not independent of each other.
